system.summary: Syllabic code of numbers 1 to about 550, one number per letter, syllable, common word or name, with homophones; written as dash- or point-separated numbers inside clear French. Made by Jean de Neufville and sent to Baudouin in March 1779.

prior_solution.where: No edition or study of this correspondence or its code was found (Founders Online, HathiTrust full text, Cryptiana; Butler's 1978 index to the Papers of the Continental Congress lists 'Van Temmel').

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.

solution.what: Found the free NARA Catalog copy of the file (file unit 464816476, 808 images) and mapped Fold3 page numbers to its frames.
Transcribed de Neufville's enciphered fair draft pp.604-606 twice and aligned it with his plain draft on p.599 (19 April 1779, 'Mad. d'Arras').

Built key K1 (139 numbers) only from his interlined drafts pp.600-603 and 609, froze it, and predicted pp.604-605: 139 of 146 covered groups as in his draft; 200 shuffled keys at most 15. Held-out pairs: 8 of 10, shuffled at most 3.
Key K2 (170 numbers) frozen with the whole 6 May 1779 draft (p.608) held out: 64 of 65 covered groups predicted; 200 shuffled keys at most 7.
Added the recipient's glosses over Baudouin's letters pp.516-548 and 579; full key 204 numbers frozen (key_full_r3.json).

Identified 'Dunoyer' as Baudouin from the leaves: letters of 25 Feb and 7 Mar 1779 signed 'Baudouin', the second saying he will in future sign a name from the enclosed little cipher; same hand later signs 'Dunoyer'.
Read the bare groups of pp.491-492 and 573 with the frozen key; two unglossed lines of p.527 decoded but not read.
Searched Founders Online, HathiTrust full text, Cryptiana and the repository for this channel or code: nothing printed.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 305 tokens, 119 types, fr-1750-nospace order 4: reading -2.099 per letter; random keys -3.504 (z 9.1); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.188 (mean -2.219, z 4.1); annealer on the real text -2.077. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.037; polyphony 0.036; 29 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.077

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The writer's own plain drafts with numbers written over them, and the recipient's glosses, give the code; a key frozen from some drafts predicts the others.

credits.note: Andrew Beling, with AI agents: free images located, the code reconstructed from de Neufville's drafts and tested on held-out drafts, 'Dunoyer' identified as Baudouin from the leaves, and the bare passages of pp.491-492 and 573 read. Not rechecked by a second agent.
Jean de Neufville, who made the code and wrote numbers over his own drafts, and glossed some of Baudouin's letters; Baudouin, who read de Neufville's letters in it.

texts.label: B573, Dunoyer (Baudouin) to de Neufville, 24 January 1780
texts.summary: The pro-British party will make the States General swallow the last pill and be shamed; someone has long since taken the loan business away from the [?]rands and given it up; a loan nobody will put money into only harms the credit of [349]; speak to 'M. du Fresne' (Chaumont).
texts.note: 39 of 43 numbers read by the key; 3, 58, 227, 349 open.

reading_review.by: Andrew Beling's own AI agents (not a person, not an outside check)
reading_review.note: Code groups decoded with the frozen key and read in the clear French of the letter; holes kept; not rechecked by a second agent.

texts.label: B491, Dunoyer (Baudouin) to de Neufville, 18 January 1780
texts.summary: On the Stadholder and the 'merry band'; V. Vort parades his intimacy with Leerding and boasts at court of successes he owes to the Pensionary of Amsterdam.
texts.note: 12 of 18 numbers read; 405, 387, 390, 447 probably nulls (12 of 14 if so).

reading_review.by: Andrew Beling's own AI agents (not a person, not an outside check)

outcome.fraction_read_source: letters/B*.txt: 56 of 68 numbers in the read passages (B491, B492, B573) have a key value; B527 (15 numbers) decoded, not read. The drafts and glossed letters were read by their writer and recipient and are not counted.

gaps.detail: Not glossed or drafted anywhere in the file; candidates in NOTES.md.

gaps.item: Full transcription of the glossed letters pp.516-548
gaps.detail: Only the gloss pairs are transcribed (key/key_pairs_classB_glosses.tsv), not the whole letters.

outcome.notes: Most coded text in the file was read at the time: de Neufville's drafts carry his plain French, and he glossed many of Baudouin's letters. What is new is the reconstruction of the code from the drafts, the identification of 'Dunoyer' as Baudouin, and the reading of the bare passages.
